stories.headline: SEBI tells market players to stop publishing IPO grey market premiums
stories.summary: SEBI asked all registered intermediaries and market participants to stop publishing or circulating grey market premium (GMP) figures for IPOs, on websites, apps, SMS or social media. It called the figures unofficial, unverified and unregulated, and warned investors that GMP-linked deals happen outside exchanges, with no settlement guarantee and no access to SEBI or exchange grievance systems.
stories.why_it_matters: GMP numbers drive a lot of retail IPO demand; curbing them could cool frenzied subscriptions and listing-day bets.

impact.why: Less GMP hype may temper retail rush and listing-day swings in new issues.

stories.headline: RBI proposes new safeguards to give customers more control over digital payments
stories.summary: The RBI issued draft rules for all types of banks that would let customers control how and how much their digital payment channels can be used. It also proposes widening what counts as negligence by a bank in fraud cases, building on its June 2026 rules limiting customer liability. Comments are open until December 14, 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: A wider definition of bank negligence could shift more fraud losses from customers to banks.

stories.headline: RBI Governor urges NBFCs and housing lenders to grow credit responsibly
stories.summary: The RBI Governor met heads of select NBFCs, housing finance companies and microfinance lenders in Mumbai on Monday, along with all four Deputy Governors. He asked them to keep credit growth sustainable, put customers first, follow fair recovery practices and tighten cyber security under board oversight.

stories.headline: Home Ministry's cyber crime centre warns WhatsApp Web users of account misuse
stories.summary: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) says a logged-in WhatsApp Web session can be misused to read and send messages as the user and run frauds on their contacts. It advises logging out after each use, avoiding public or borrowed computers and not sharing sensitive or official information over WhatsApp Web.

stories.headline: Iran's IRGC says three tankers caught fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers struck naval mines over several hours in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, two of them while under US air escort. They gave no ship names, crew details or damage reports, and no independent maritime source has confirmed it. Qatar's prime minister told Al Jazeera the region cannot withstand another US-Iran escalation. Brent was slightly lower in Asia at about $86.3.
stories.why_it_matters: If confirmed, attacks on escorted tankers would raise the risk to Gulf oil flows that India depends on.
stories.note: Claim by Iran's IRGC; not independently confirmed.

impact.why: An attack on escorted tankers would raise supply risk, though Brent has not reacted so far.

stories.headline: EU proposes 22nd Russia sanctions package, cutting 60 banks from SWIFT
stories.summary: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed new sanctions that would cut 60 Russian banks off the SWIFT payments system, set up a task force on crypto used to dodge sanctions and bar Russian teams and athletes from competing under Russia's flag at EU events. All 27 member states must approve it before it takes effect.

stories.headline: US blacklists Singapore's Megaspeed and six other Asian firms over chip exports
stories.summary: The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security added Singapore-based Megaspeed International and six firms in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List, so US suppliers now need a licence to ship them advanced tech such as top Nvidia AI chips. BIS said they acted against US security or foreign policy interests. Megaspeed is linked to the probe surrounding Nvidia.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera, citing the BIS Federal Register filing.

stories.headline: Dollar index eases to about 104.2 in Asia; yen near 158.8 before US PCE data
stories.summary: The dollar index slipped about 0.1% to near 104.2 in early Asian trade after Monday's jump, while the dollar held near 158.8 yen and the euro edged up to about $1.092. FXStreet says the euro hit its lowest since April 2025 on Monday. Traders now look to Wednesday's core PCE inflation data, the next test for a December Fed hike. The onshore rupee last closed at 92.92 on Monday; Indian stock markets are shut today for Gurpurab.
stories.why_it_matters: A firm PCE reading would cement a Fed hike and keep pressure on the rupee.
stories.note: Levels from Yahoo Finance; euro low per FXStreet. Not confirmed by a core trusted outlet.

impact.why: Dollar is pausing near 104 as traders await Wednesday's US inflation data.

stories.headline: Asia chip stocks soar: Taiwan up 9%, Kospi 7% after Nvidia's 31% jump
stories.summary: Asian markets followed Wall Street's surge after Nvidia rehired Jensen Huang as CEO. Taiwan's index rose about 9% and South Korea's Kospi about 7% to above 5,000, triggering a trading sidecar, while Japan's Nikkei, shut on Monday, gained about 4%. TSMC, Foxconn, MediaTek and SK Hynix rose near 10%, Samsung about 8%, and Advantest and Tokyo Electron 12-15%. Nvidia closed up 31% on Monday, adding about $950 billion in value.
stories.why_it_matters: The global AI-chip rebound could lift sentiment and IT and tech shares when Indian markets reopen on Wednesday.

image.alt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang smiling and waving outdoors

impact.why: A strong global tech rebound tends to lift Indian IT shares.
Chip rally extends into Asia, supporting AI and semiconductor stocks.

stories.headline: Update: Nasdaq closes 6.5% higher in best day since April 2025; S&P up 4.7%
stories.summary: At the close, the S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237.17, the Nasdaq 6.5% to 24,089.56 and the Dow 3% to 49,595.31, recovering from Friday's slide into correction. S&P tech stocks gained about 9%; Micron rose 19%, CoreWeave 22% and Tesla about 11%. US stock futures were up a further 0.3% in Asia.
stories.note: Update: final closing levels; the previous edition had early-session figures.

impact.why: Biggest one-day tech rally in 19 months as AI fears ease.

stories.headline: Gold holds near $3,664 and Brent slips to $86.3 in Asian trade
stories.summary: US gold futures were about 0.35% higher at around $3,664 an ounce early Tuesday, holding Monday's 4% rebound. Brent crude eased about 0.45% to near $86.3 a barrel, little moved by Iran's claim of tanker mine hits. Silver futures were up about 0.4% at about $43.3.
stories.note: Single source: Yahoo Finance price data.

impact.why: Gold steadies after its rebound as the dollar eases slightly.

stories.headline: BridgeBio wins first-ever US approval for a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy drug
stories.summary: The FDA gave full approval to BridgeBio's Welgemda (ribitol), a daily oral pill, as the first treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, days ahead of its November 27 deadline. In the Phase 3 FORTIFY trial it improved walking speed and lung function over 12 months against placebo. BridgeBio plans an immediate US launch; about 7,000 people in the US and Europe have the condition or related disorders.
stories.why_it_matters: It is the first approved therapy for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, which until now was only managed for symptoms.

impact.why: First-in-class full approval with an immediate launch and a priority review voucher.
